title: a Result PARAMETER whose only consumption is an unwrap inside a callback body is consumed, exactly as a local binding is
notes: specification/failures.mdx:190: 'A Result MUST be treated as a must-use value. A source program MUST NOT silently discard a Result without returning, matching, transforming, inspecting, or unwrapping it.' `entry` is unwrapped with postfix `!`, which is one of the five named acts, and the sentence conditions none of them on the function body the act is written in. 07-must-consume/result-parameter-must-be-consumed pins the refusal direction — a Result parameter nothing consumes is SMITHERS1302 — and this is its acceptance direction for a consumption that happens one function deeper. The printed line comes from `main` rather than from `forward`: the promise this case pins is that the program COMPILES, and `forward` cannot be called from authored `.sm` at all, because handing a Result to a user function is not consumption and the argument would be charged at its producer (07-must-consume/handing-a-result-collection-to-a-user-function-is-not-consumption). DELIBERATELY PAIRED with a-result-consumed-only-inside-a-callback-is-consumed, which is the identical consumption site reached from a local binding and which BOTH backends accept. RETIRED XFAIL (go): the fork reported SMITHERS1302@14:25 on a parameter that `entry!` consumes one line later. The cause was the one the marker named — `checkResultParameters` ran a hand-rolled walk of the function BODY that halted at every nested function-like, so the fork was inconsistent with itself: it accepted the byte-equivalent program in which `entry` is a local binding, because the binding rule asks a per-file identifier index keyed by resolved SYMBOL. The parameter walk now asks that same index (`identifierReferences`), which is the fourth caller rather than a fifth private walk. A shadowing declaration in a nested scope resolves to a different symbol, so the wider search cannot manufacture a consumption the narrow one would have missed. THE CLASS WAS MEASURED, not assumed, and it had a second member nobody had recorded: because the old walk started at the body, a Result parameter consumed in a SIBLING PARAMETER'S DEFAULT was unreachable too — probed before the fix, the reference ran and printed while the fork reported SMITHERS1302@10:22, and both agree after it. The fork has five recursive walks that halt at a nested function-like; the other four halt correctly — `collectTopProvides`, `checkTopLevelRequirements` and `checkTopLevelCheckedChannels` are module-evaluation passes for which descending would be wrong, and `collectFacts` stops because a nested function is its own row. This was the only OWNERSHIP walk among them, and the only one that was wrong.
